articles.title: The curious case of Kelsey Plum: WNBA star who gave up $1.4M deal and asked for exactly $999,999— nobody knows why it’s one dollar short of $1m
articles.summary: International Sports News: Explore the intriguing story behind Kelsey Plum's contract with the Los Angeles Sparks, where she opted for a quirky $999,999 salary instead of a million, leaving fans and analysts speculating about her decision. Investigate the implications of this choice and its effects on her team's future.
articles.body: There was nothing particularly unusual about Kelsey Plum agreeing to stay in Los Angeles for another season. The strange part was the number attached to the deal. When the details emerged, the Sparks guard had agreed to a salary of exactly $999,999, leaving one very conspicuous dollar missing from what could have been a much cleaner $1 million.Kelsey Plum deliberately stopped at $999,999Plum agreed to a one-year contract with the Los Angeles Sparks on April 12, 2026, shortly after a strong first season in Los Angeles had put her in position for a substantial new deal.The 31-year-old had arrived with the Sparks after the major three-team trade involving the Las Vegas Aces, Seattle Storm and Los Angeles, in which Plum went to Los Angeles, Jewell Loyd moved to Las Vegas and Seattle acquired the rights to the No. 2 pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft, which became Dominique Malonga, along with additional draft picks changing hands.Plum settled in quickly, she averaged 19.5 points per game during her first season with the Sparks and helped the team enjoy its best campaign since 2020. With the new WNBA Collective Bargaining Agreement subsequently raising salaries across the league, Plum had been eligible for a veteran supermax worth as much as $1.4 million.Instead, she signed for exactly $999,999.The difference between the figure on the contract and the round number was only $1, but Plum had actually agreed to leave roughly $400,000 of potential salary on the table.Plum wanted to give Los Angeles additional room under the salary cap to build a stronger team around her, with the aim of turning the Sparks into a genuine championship contender.At the time, however, the missing dollar was what caught everybody's attention.Plum eventually explained the missing dollarThe mystery lasted only a few weeks before Plum was asked about it directly.In an interview with YouTuber Austin Franklin, Plum explained why she had stopped at $999,999 rather than accepting an even $1 million.Her first answer was straightforward.“I mean, first of all, taxes,” Plum said.“If you claim a million dollars, I saved $13,000 [in taxes] in not claiming a dollar.”Plum then explained that the decision had taken on a life of its own after the contract became public.“It's funny, everywhere I go now, people are like, 'Hey, can I give you a dollar?'” Plum said. “I think it's great. They're tuned in, you know?”She then offered another reason for deliberately staying below the seven-figure mark.“And the other thing was just like, I didn't want validation for signing for a million. It was like, I don't need to sign for a million to know my value as a player. It was a combination of that, but really more the taxes.”That explanation made the $999,999 figure considerably more interesting, because Plum was not simply trying to create a funny contract number. She said she had made a conscious decision to avoid crossing the $1 million threshold.There was just one problem with the way she described the tax saving.The $13,000 tax saving did not work quite like thatThe tax explanation quickly attracted attention from people who pointed out that California's so-called “millionaire's tax” does not work by suddenly taxing an entire salary at 13 per cent once a player reaches $1 million.California currently has the highest top marginal income tax rate in the United States, reaching 13.3 per cent on income above $1 million. The important word is marginal: the higher rate applies to the income above the relevant threshold rather than retroactively applying to every dollar earned.Entrepreneur and sports-business content creator Joe Pompliano was among those to challenge Plum's calculation.“Someone please explain marginal tax rates to Kelsey Plum. If she earned one more dollar, she would be taxed 13 cents…not $13,000. And even if that were true, she is ignoring jock taxes, endorsement income, etc,” Pompliano wrote.In other words, moving from $999,999 to $1 million would not, by itself, create a $13,000 California tax bill. On the simplified example, the additional dollar reaching the threshold would generate roughly 13 cents of tax at a 13 per cent marginal rate, rather than suddenly exposing the entire $1 million to that rate.The situation can become more complicated for professional athletes because their overall taxable income can include money from endorsements and income earned in different jurisdictions, but the basic marginal-tax principle remains the same.So while Plum's decision to stay one dollar below $1 million was real, the specific $13,000 saving she cited was not supported by the marginal-rate calculation described by tax commentators.Plum gave up much more than one dollarThe tax debate made the $999,999 figure even more memorable, but the bigger financial decision was hiding in plain sight.Plum was eligible for a $1.4 million veteran supermax, meaning she could have earned substantially more than the amount written into her contract.Instead, she accepted $999,999 and gave the Sparks more flexibility to improve the roster.That sacrifice fitted with what Plum said about not needing a seven-figure salary to validate her worth as a player. The decision was also tied to the larger ambition she had for Los Angeles after helping the Sparks produce their best season in several years.Whether the Sparks ultimately built the championship-level roster Plum had hoped for became a separate question during the 2026 season.The curious contract, meanwhile, did not last quite as long as Plum might have expected.In August 2026, just months after signing the deal, Plum was traded to the Phoenix Mercury.The $999,999 contract had therefore already become more than a quirky number. It was a snapshot of a moment when Plum wanted to stay in Los Angeles, believed in what the Sparks could build and was willing to take less money to help make it happen.And, for reasons that will probably keep the dollar joke alive for a while, she made sure the number stopped at $999,999 rather than $1 million.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: L.A. Olympics chairman Casey Wasserman takes $5.1 million hit on futuristic mansion after listing it for $32.5 million and making multiple price cuts
articles.summary: International Sports News: Casey Wasserman closed the door on his futuristic Hollywood Hills home. The numbers, however, were not what he expected. The chairman of the 2028 Los .
articles.body: Casey Wasserman closed the door on his futuristic Hollywood Hills home. The numbers, however, were not what he expected. The chairman of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics sold his award-winning Bird Streets estate for $18.5 million, a steep comedown from the $32.5 million he originally asked for it.The sale caps months of markdowns on a house once celebrated for its design. It also lands at an odd moment for the 52-year-old sports and entertainment mogul, whose name has been tied to headlines that have nothing to do with real estate.Casey Wasserman sells futuristic mansion at a major lossCasey Wasserman listed the property in September 2025, five years after it won the AIA Los Angeles Award for the city's most influential architecture. Buyers weren't rushing in. By February, he had shaved $2.6 million off the price, dropping it to $29.9 million. Still, it wasn't enough, so the number fell again, this time to $24.9 million.Realtor.com reports the home eventually sold for $18.5 million. Wasserman had paid $23.6 million for it back in August 2020, which puts his loss on the deal at roughly $5.1 million. It was a heavy hit.Inside the Bird Streets estate that inspired the lossThe house sits on what the listing calls the most prime cul-de-sac in Bird Streets, one of the most exclusive pockets of the Hollywood Hills. Designed by XTEN Architects, the place draws heavily from Stanley Kubrick's "2001: A Space Odyssey," right down to ceilings that reportedly cost more than $1 million to build.Five bedrooms and seven bathrooms fill roughly 12,000 square feet, and the primary suite leans into a dark, moody look with glass walls that pull in light and sweeping views. A wall installation inside reads "More, Faster, Now," while an eight-car underground garage sits below a home that also includes a private theater, a dance studio, and an infinity pool overlooking the hillside.It's a far cry from the last mansion Wasserman parted with. In June 2020, he sold his custom Beverly Hills estate, the Foothill Estate, to music executive David Geffen for $68 million. That home was built where his grandfather, the late entertainment titan Lew Wasserman, once lived, and it had originally been listed for $125 million.Did Casey Wasserman's controversy impact the sale?The sale comes months after Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass publicly called for Wasserman to step down as LA28 chairman. Her reasoning traced back to emails between Wasserman and Ghislaine Maxwell that surfaced in Department of Justice files released in February 2026. Bass didn't hold back when asked about it, telling CNN, "My opinion is that he should step down."Wasserman has said his contact with Maxwell and Jeffrey Epstein amounted to one humanitarian trip to Africa in 2002 and a handful of emails he now regrets. The LA28 board's executive committee reviewed the matter and sided with him, stating that his relationship with the pair "did not go beyond what has already been publicly documented." He kept his post.Whether the controversy nudged buyers away from the mansion is impossible to say for certain. But the timing, arriving in the same stretch as the price cuts, hasn't gone unnoticed.Casey Wasserman had another financial hit involving his talent agencyThe house wasn't the only asset Wasserman put up for sale this year. Days after the LA28 committee finished its review, he told staff at his talent agency, Wasserman, that he had begun selling the company. In his memo, he wrote that he had become a distraction to its work and said Mike Watts would take over daily operations while he focused on the Olympics.The fallout from the Maxwell emails had already cost the agency clients. Chappell Roan, Odesza, Orville Peck, and retired soccer star Abby Wambach all cut ties. By July 2026, the agency was working toward a buyout of Wasserman's stake backed by Providence Equity Partners, with Watts stepping in as CEO and Providence taking majority ownership.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Carrying India’s basketball dream to Asian Games, referee Rakesh to make his Asiad debut even as no Indian team will take court
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: CHENNAI: While India has no basketball team at the Asian Games, R Rakesh is the country’s sole representative in the sport as a referee. The Aichi-Nag.
articles.body: CHENNAI: While India has no basketball team at the Asian Games, R Rakesh is the country’s sole representative in the sport as a referee. The Aichi-Nagoya Games will mark his debut in Asian Games, the Karnataka man earlier appearing for Asian championships.The 36-year-old became a FIBA referee at the age of 23 and has a vast experience for over a decade. “Till now (in the current edition), I have officiated on almost all the days. At the Asian Championships last year in China, I officiated until the semifinals. Since it was my maiden edition, I could not proceed further. There have been many ups and downs in my journey. In some tournaments, I get to officiate in the final, but in some, I do not even get to officiate in the semifinals. It depends on the performance, and that is common in sports,” Rakesh told TOI from Japan.Rakesh, currently India’s only elite-level referee, said lack of monetary benefit is one of the reasons behind the lack of quality Indian officials. “How long can a referee manage to officiate in matches without much monetary benefit? Passion can only push a person to a certain point. Why do people prefer cricket? It is because of the monetary benefits. We need to have leagues, more international matches in India and popularise the sport....Initially, I also struggled and used to do only domestic matches. Sometimes, tournaments used to get cancelled in rainy seasons and at times due to lack of sponsorships the tournaments got scrapped. However, now I get to officiate regularly,” Rakesh added.Rakesh has officiated in multiple leagues across Asia, including in the Philippines, Lebanon, Syria and Indonesia. He has also been officiating in the Maldives league for the past 10 years. In 2018, he received an opportunity to officiate at the World Junior NBA Championships in Miami.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Seven months pregnant, she judged bouts. Now, history awaits Kirtisna at 2026 Asian Games
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: There is one image from her wrestling journey that Kirtisna Arya remembers with unusual clarity. It was May 2023. She was in Phnom Penh, Ca.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: There is one image from her wrestling journey that Kirtisna Arya remembers with unusual clarity. It was May 2023. She was in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, for the South East Asian (SEA) Games, seven months pregnant with her second child.While most expectant mothers would have been preparing for the final stretch of pregnancy, Kirtisna was spending five consecutive days on a wrestling mat, demonstrating her officiating and judging skills as part of her United World Wrestling (UWW) coaching examination.The examination could not wait. Neither could she. “I was seven months pregnant (with son Darsh) was when I appeared for the Category 1 Level 1 course. For four-five days continuously, I had to be on the mat and demonstrate my skills. I was pregnant, but I was determined to complete the course,” Kirtisna recalls.That determination, more than three years later, has taken the 37-year-old from Uttarakhand to Nagoya — Kirtisna will become the first Indian woman to officiate at the Games, or any of the other major multisport events.Accredited as technical official, Kirtisna will shoulder three responsibilities during the Games: referee bouts, judge matches and serve as mat chairman.“When I received the mail from UWW informing me about my selection, it was a proud moment for the family. My daughter Pannavi was overjoyed,” Kirtisna told TOI.“I never thought I would be selected for the Asian Games,” she said.Krirtisna will leave for Japan on Sept 26. The assignment will keep her away from home for around 10 days, including from three-and-a-half-year-old Darsh. “I know it will be difficult for them, but they will understand what their mother did when they grow up and hopefully take pride in it,” she said.For Kirtisna, the road to Japan has never been about reaching one particular destination. It has been about refusing to step away from wrestling — even when life repeatedly gave her reasons to do so.Kirtisna grew up in Bharatpur village in Haridwar district, in a family where wrestling was deeply woven into everyday life. Father Omveer Singh was a renowned wrestler and a disciple of the legendary Master Chandgi Ram. Yet having a wrestler for a father did not necessarily make it easy for the daughters to become wrestlers. “People would say, ‘Girls are not meant for wrestling. Don’t put your girls there.’ There was a lot of societal pressure,” Kirtisna says.Yet, Kirtisna, the second of three sisters, began wrestling in 2004 after Class X, and her biggest achievement on the mat came at the 2011 Commonwealth Championships in Melbourne, where she won silver in the 59kg category.An ACL tear brought end to her playing career and she quit wrestling in 2013. She completed an NIS coaching diploma in 2010-11 and, in Feb 2014, joined the SAI centre in Bahalgarh, Sonepat, as an assistant coach. Motherhood brought a fresh challenge. Her daughter Pannavi was born in 2016 and that led her to switch to refereeing.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: No breakfast! Chaotic start for Indian athletes ahead of Asian Games
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: BENGALURU: Indian athletics contingent that landed in Japan ahead of the Asian Games had a harrowing time, waiting more than four hours for check-in a.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Indian athletics contingent that landed in Japan ahead of the Asian Games had a harrowing time, waiting more than four hours for check-in after reaching the hotel at 10 am, local time, on Sunday. The men’s and women’s teams and the coaches are accommodated in three different hotels which are more than four km away from the training facility at Tsukuba.On Monday, the men’s contingent was shocked when their hotel staff informed them that no breakfast had been booked for them.“The entire men’s squad didn’t get breakfast at the hotel. The hotel staff stated they had not received notification to serve breakfast to the athletes. Many athletes went without food that morning. Few of them went out and managed to grab a bite but this exposed a lack of planning by the officials deputed by the Athletics Federation of India (AFI),” sources told TOI. “The athletes faced another problem on Monday evening when the designated bus didn’t come to pick them up for the training session.”They also said that they had to travel four kms for lunch and dinner. The Japanese hotel provided rice and soybeans for breakfast.“There is no special diet — no fruit (which is expensive in Japan). At the Indian restaurant, they were served rice, roti and chicken,” sources added. The Indian athletics contingent landed in the Japanese city to make their final preparations at the University of Tsukuba ground.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: From uplifting heartbroken team to calling out Chess Olympiad hotel mess: Srinath is India's man to count on
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: It was the final round of the Global Chess League (GCL) round-robin last Saturday in Bengaluru, and American Gambits needed a big win, with.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: It was the final round of the Global Chess League (GCL) round-robin last Saturday in Bengaluru, and American Gambits needed a big win, with an eight-point margin, to reach the final. Mumba Masters were the opponents. As the match wore on, the Gambits, playing with Black, went all out. Javokhir Sindarov, playing on the Icon board, won his game. On the next board, Indian grandmaster Nihal Sarin had an early advantage, which translated almost into a winning position. But then, calamity struck.The clock ran out. Sarin lost on time. His team lost with him.The next moment, Nihal was pressed against the side glass of the dugout, face to the panel, looking as though the gates might open and the tears might come at any second. Then he felt a palm settle lightly on his shoulder. It was none other than the Gambits' captain and coach, Srinath Narayanan."It was very painful," Srinath told TimesofIndia.com later during an exclusive interaction. "You usually need some time and space for the emotions to dial down. And I think that's pretty much the only thing that can heal things."There was no tactical debrief that night, no post-mortem of the time scramble. Srinath took the squad out for a team dinner instead. Later, back at the hotel, they pulled out board games, like Salem and Avalon, and played into the night."We tried to take our minds off these things," Srinath recalled with a smile. "And then at night, we played some fun games that helped us cope with it."The response the next day suggested it had worked. Facing the same Mumba Masters in the third-place match, the Gambits crushed them across both legs. Nihal won both his games. The Gambits took bronze.Srinath was there; he is here too"We are overall quite happy, because it would have been very depressing and disappointing if we had lost today," Srinath said, acknowledging his team's performance in GCL 2026. "But it also feels like a slight underachievement given the potential of the team.""We felt like we were definitely one of the contenders for winning the tournament. And we played that way for the most part. So we just lost out on those last two matches, where things got decided at the very end, in the last few seconds."This is a man who knows what winning a team event actually looks like and what it takes to do so. When India took gold in Budapest at the 2024 Olympiad, Srinath was there.He was there, too, on Tuesday, when the Indian contingent landed in Samarkand for the 46th Olympiad and found themselves stranded without accommodation. And he was the first to break the silence publicly."Having a terrible experience at the FIDE 2026 Olympiad," he wrote on X. "The team landed 5 hours ago at Samarkand airport. The team still haven't been allotted rooms, with absolutely no clarity on when it'll be allotted."As TimesofIndia.com reported later in the evening, the players were eventually given individual rooms. The coaching staff were put into shared rooms for the time being.When the suspense over India's board order finally lifted, the team going with a straight rating-wise arrangement, putting Praggnanandhaa (2761) on Board 1, Arjun Erigaisi (2759) on Board 2, Nihal (2718) on Board 3, D Gukesh (2703) on Board 4 and Vidit Gujrathi (2697) on Board 5, Srinath took to X again, this time with rather more mischief."Don't blame me for keeping the board order in suspense. I had it on chess-results right from September 1," he penned.The captain on India's Olympiad prepPreparation for the Olympiad had already begun well before the GCL gig, in the form of a virtual camp with the full squad.When asked how it went, he replied, "It went really well. As a unit, we gelled really well. The players are all around similar ages. And we have Vidit, who is quite experienced but still not quite that old."One of the sources of encouragement for the 32-year-old Grandmaster was that three of his Olympiad squad, Nihal, Arjun and Vidit, had all been in Bengaluru, and all three finished with positive scores in the tournament."It's pretty encouraging that the three players who are here played quite well," Srinath told this website. "All of them with positive scores. I think that's also an encouraging sign for the team."In general, the fact that we can all be friends with each other, we can have a fun time even outside of the tournament, I think that's a really special thing about Olympiad."From rapid back to classicalThere is one obvious wrinkle in going straight from a rapid-format league into the sport's biggest classical team event. And Srinath doesn't dismiss it."It definitely can take a game or two to get back," he admitted. "But it won't take longer than that."In general, at the Olympiad, the first few rounds are not the most challenging rounds. So it gives us plenty of time to acclimatise."And the composition of his squad helps more."The younger you are, the easier it is to adapt," he said, a useful trait in a team where four of the five boards are occupied by players in their early twenties or younger.ALSO READ: The silver medal Koneru Humpy's 9-year-old daughter will remember as goldSrinath has spent this fortnight uplifting a devastated dressing room, calling out a governing body over a logistical mess, and cheekily reminding everyone on social media that he'd had India's board order published for weeks.In Samarkand, this is the man India counts on to do all of it again.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: What did Adam Silver tell Sophie Cunningham? Fever guard reveals details of private call with NBA boss
articles.summary: International Sports News: Sophie Cunningham picked up the phone recently and found NBA commissioner Adam Silver on the other end, wanting her honest read on what the WNBA needs.
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham picked up the phone recently and found NBA commissioner Adam Silver on the other end, wanting her honest read on what the WNBA needs in its next leader. The Indiana Fever guard confirmed the call took place, though she kept most of it close, choosing instead to speak in broad terms about the kind of person she thinks should take over from Cathy Engelbert.Talking with reporters after practice, Cunningham didn't hand Silver a shortlist of names. She laid out a vision instead, one built around unity and genuine access for players, a pointed nod to what many around the league feel has been missing during Engelbert's run at the top.Sophie Cunningham reveals conversation with Adam SilverSophie Cunningham addressed the call on Monday, a few days after Engelbert announced she would step down at the end of 2026. Silver is expected to lead the search for her replacement, since the WNBA commissioner answers directly to him. Neither the league nor Cunningham confirmed exactly what was said between the two, but the fact that Silver reached out to a player at all says something about how much her voice carries these days.“I think the WNBA has always been a place for people to feel safe and comfortable. I think there’s all types of walks in this organization, or in this league, which I think is absolutely awesome. But I do think with that you need someone who’s going to unite everybody because it can be so different. But that doesn’t mean it’s a bad thing. I think it makes it a lot of fun,” Cunningham said.Cunningham, 30, has become one of the more talked-about figures in the league this year, largely because of her outspoken stance on transgender athletes competing in women's sports. That position has drawn protests at road games and turned her into a polarizing figure for some fans. Whatever friction it's created outside the arena, it clearly hasn't stopped Silver from valuing her input on league matters that go well beyond the court.She didn't put forward any specific candidates for the job, saying she trusts Silver and his team to make that call. What she did offer was a clear picture of the qualities she wants in whoever takes the role next.Why Cunningham wants a WNBA commissioner who unites the leagueThe 6-foot-1 guard was direct about what matters most to her. She wants someone capable of bringing together a locker room, and a league, that includes a wide range of personalities and perspectives. "You need someone who's going to unite everybody," Cunningham said, framing that difference as a strength rather than a problem.Engelbert has faced criticism for keeping her distance from players, and Cunningham shared that she wants the opposite from the next commissioner: someone willing to build real relationships with the athletes, even when that means delivering decisions players won't love. An open line of communication, she argued, changes how those tough calls land.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'If you want to make any changes, this is the right time': PR Sreejesh ahead of Asiad 2026
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: KOLKATA: With the Indian men’s hockey team preparing to defend its Asian Games title, former captain and goalkeeper PR Sreejesh believes the next two .
articles.body: KOLKATA: With the Indian men’s hockey team preparing to defend its Asian Games title, former captain and goalkeeper PR Sreejesh believes the next two years will be crucial not just for winning in Asia but for building a team capable of challenging the world’s best at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.Sreejesh said the period following the Asian Games would present the ideal opportunity to make changes to the squad and gradually integrate younger players into the senior setup. “If you want to make any changes, this is the right time,” Sreejesh told TOI in an exclusive interview.“Next year we play the Pro League, some Test matches and maybe Azlan Shah Trophy. Then the year after, it’s going to be the same set of matches. So, after the Asian Games and the Hockey India League, this is the right time to change the core group or the coaching staff. Then it becomes easier to focus on a two-year cycle and build a new team with a new support staff.”The two-time Olympic medallist, who is currently working in Kerala’s Education Department, also felt India’s disappointing World Cup campaign should serve as a reality check despite the team’s dominance in Asia.“Asian hockey is not the benchmark. If we are realistically thinking about 2028, we need to look at where we stand against the best teams in the world,” he said. “Beating a top team once in a tournament is not enough. We need consistency.”While backing India to retain the Asian Games crown, where they are in Group A, alongside Japan, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and Indonesia, Sreejesh cautioned against conceding avoidable goals and squandering opportunities at the other end.“If the opposition scores through a brilliant move, you can appreciate that. But conceding goals through silly mistakes is like killing yourself,” he added. “At the same time, getting chances and not converting them is equally costly. We just need to be sharper and do the simple things in the best way possible.”The former India custodian, meanwhile, had a message for the two goalkeepers, Mohith HS and Suraj Karkera, ahead of the continental tournament. Communication, he said, would be key, but equally important would be the ability to quickly move on after mistakes.Recalling advice from one of his own goalkeeping coaches, he added: “A goalkeeper should be like a duck. When water falls on a duck, it just rolls off. Goals should be the same. Whether you concede one or make a save, it shouldn’t stay with you. It should drain out immediately. That’s the mentality a goalkeeper needs.”Looking ahead, Sreejesh, who coached the Indian men’s junior team to a bronze medal at the 2025 Junior World Cup, also underlined the need to create a smoother pathway from junior to senior hockey, warning against leaving a vacuum once the current core group moves on.“The players are doing their job. The system has to do its job. We need to integrate youngsters into the senior setup and give them opportunities to progress at the international level,” said Sreejesh, who recently completed the FIH Level 4 coaching course in Belgium.Despite calling for a longer-term focus on the Olympic cycle, Sreejesh remained confident about India’s immediate prospects. “For the Asian level, I think we are good enough to win. The team doesn’t need to do anything extraordinary. They just need to play their natural game,” he said.But even as he expects India to dominate at the Asiad, he believes the tournament should also mark the beginning of the team’s road to Los Angeles 2028, with an eye on building a squad capable of consistently competing with the world’s best.Tune-In: Watch Asian Games 2026 live and exclusive on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: It's Japan time: A gold double in cricket appears a given, but it will provide benchmark for LA Olympics
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: When the United States men’s basketball team goes to the Olympics, they face a unique situation. For the NBA superstars, a gold is a given, anything l.
articles.body: When the United States men’s basketball team goes to the Olympics, they face a unique situation. For the NBA superstars, a gold is a given, anything less is a fall from grace.The Indian cricket contingent at the Asian Games will feel a bit like the ‘Dream Teams’. Two gold medals appear a foregone conclusion and there would probably be any euphoria when it happens. But just in case it’s a silver for either of the star-studded teams which are products of the cash-rich IPL and WPL, the backlash will be quite significant.On the face of it, there’s no reason for any worry for those who will be tracking the Indian teams. The men have got a bye in the first round and their first match is a quarterfinal — in all probability against Nepal. If all goes to plan, Sri Lanka and Pakistan will be their next two rivals at the Korogi Sports Park — the ground built from scratch.Matches will be day games with Indian men’s matches starting at 1.30 pm local time. While Nepal is a bit of an unknown quantity, the other teams get beaten by India as a matter of habit across tournaments, be it the T20 World Cup, Asia Cup or the rare bilateral tournament.Despite the tag of overwhelming favourites, the sports ministry and the BCCI aren’t taking any chances. There was the option of sending a second-string team, but even Jasprit Bumrah, coming back from an injury lay-off, is headed to Japan. There were issues about five-star accommodation for the superstars, but that too has been taken care of to keep all the parties happy.While there’s the obligation of winning gold, there’s another angle to this Indian campaign. Cricket will be back in the Olympics at Los Angeles two years down the line after a gap of 128 years, and the success of the return hinges on how India perform.It is the Indian diaspora around the world that fuels the sport and such has been the domination of the Men in Blue in T20 cricket of late, that anything other than the champions’ medal is a huge dampener for this group of globe-trotting cheerleaders.Many of them will be at Aichi-Nagoya as well and in addition to the gold, there will be another demand from them — to witness some Vaibhav Sooryavanshi blitzkrieg.With the next T20 World Cup and the Olympics still a couple of years away, this Asian Games can also be a bit of a test for two T20 specialists Shivam Dube and Varun Chakravarthy, provided the spinner passes the fitness test following the side strain that he suffered during the Afghanistan series. They have been a slight up and down of late and there’s a chance that if they don’t get their acts right, this could be their last Indian stints for the time being.But before the men start their campaign, it’s the girls who will get the ball rolling. The women’s tournament will be a good indication as to how the conditions will be in this new venue. Harmanpreet Kaur’s girls are going to Japan on the back of a crushing Asia Cup victory, where they have walked past all the teams.There’s no reason to believe anything different will happen at Aichi-Nagoya as the men and women will look to lend a golden hue to the Indian campaign in addition to adding new fans for the sport itself with their dynamism.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: For Harmanpreet Kaur, the Asian Games will be about more than defending a gold medal. It will be another opportunity for the India captain to lead fro.
articles.body: For Harmanpreet Kaur, the Asian Games will be about more than defending a gold medal. It will be another opportunity for the India captain to lead from the front.Four years ago in Hangzhou, Harmanpreet led India to their maiden Asian Games gold, beating Sri Lanka in the final. In Japan, the skipper will be expected to marshal her resources once again as India look to retain the title and add another medal to a growing collection.The Asia Cup in the UAE did not quite go to plan for Harmanpreet with the bat, returning 71 runs in five matches, but India finished the tournament as champions. The skipper will hope to put that campaign behind her and rediscover her rhythm in Japan, particularly with a demanding season ahead.For Harmanpreet, however, the Asian Games carry a significance beyond individual numbers. Cricket offers its players a rare chance to be part of the larger Indian contingent at a multi-sport event — something they do not experience during the regular international calendar.“This is one such moment when you get your own medal and I think when it’s about the medals, the motivation increases even more. Day and night we keep thinking how we will feel after winning the medal and how we will celebrate,” Harmanpreet recently said.With cricket now set to make its return to the Olympics at Los Angeles in 2028, the Asian Games also form part of a larger journey for the India captain. At 37, Harmanpreet remains central to India’s plans and will be keen to use the Games to build momentum.Her leadership, big-match temperament and ability to change a game with the bat make her the player to watch as India chase another gold in Japan.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: The Asian Games 2026 will bring together athletes from across the continent in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with the event scheduled from September 19 to October 4. A total of 45 countries and regions are set to compete across 43 sports.India will enter the continental event after a record medal haul at Hangzhou 2023, where the country collected 107 medals, including 28 gold, 38 silver and 41 bronze.The Indian contingent will feature five individual Olympic medallists despite Neeraj Chopra withdrawing from the Games following an ankle injury. PV Sindhu, Manu Bhaker, Lovlina Borgohain, Aman Sehrawat and Mirabai Chanu are among the prominent names in the squad.Cricket will see India defend both its men's and women's titles. Shreyas Iyer will captain the men's T20 side, which includes teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, while Harmanpreet Kaur will lead the women's team.Hockey will also carry significant importance because the men's and women's competitions will double up as continental qualification events for the LA 2028 Olympics. The Asian Games winners in both hockey tournaments will earn direct qualification for LA 2028.Anahat Singh returns after helping India secure a women's team bronze and a mixed doubles bronze with Abhay Singh at Hangzhou 2023. articles.title: 'Athletes got an experience to stay in containers': Sharath Kamal on Asian Games accommodation challenge
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: India’s deputy chef-de-mission for the Asian Games, Achanta Sharath Kamal, believes Indian athletes will have little trouble adjusting to the unusual .
articles.body: India’s deputy chef-de-mission for the Asian Games, Achanta Sharath Kamal, believes Indian athletes will have little trouble adjusting to the unusual accommodation arrangements at the Aichi-Nagoya Games, despite concerns raised by some participating countries.India’s 501 athletes and 265 officials will stay in a mix of converted shipping containers, a docked cruise ship and hotels when the Games begin on September 19. While the container rooms have been criticised as cramped, Sharath said Indian athletes have already had some experience of staying in similar facilities."For the players, by the direction of the Sports Authority of India, we have had some containers built in various SAI campuses, where the athletes got an experience to stay in containers. And of course, cruise ships, we tried to replicate something like that," said Sharath, as quoted by news agency PTI.Around 4,000-5,000 athletes will stay on the luxury cruise liner Costa Serena at Nagoya Port, while around 2,000 will be housed in converted shipping containers at Garden Pier in Nagoya Bay. The rest will stay in hotels near competition venues in Aichi and, for some events such as swimming, in Tokyo.Athletes prepared for the challengeSharath, who is also the vice chair of the Athletes Commission of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), said the bigger concern was for officials, who did not get the same opportunity as athletes to experience the makeshift accommodation beforehand."But at the same time, players know what to expect. We have educated them very well. And I am pretty sure they will get accustomed quite quickly," he said."The important thing is the performance. I am sure they will be able to perform well."At least one TT medalSharath is also expecting India’s table tennis team to return with at least one medal. The 10-member squad includes five men and five women, with the men's doubles pair of Manav Thakkar and Manush Shah and the mixed doubles combination of Manush and Diya Chitale among India's medal hopes."My expectation is to win at least one medal, if not two. Last time, we got one medal in women's double. And prior to that, we got two bronze medals in 2018," Sharath said."The men's doubles pair of Manush and Manav, they are doing extremely well. They were world number two at one point in time. They are in the top four now. And they have a good chance of winning a medal," said the 44-year-old."So these two events, we have a good chance to win medals. And of course, team championships are always quite an open event."Table tennis competitions will be held from September 20 to 28.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Commanders' defender 'uncertain' for Week 2 matchup vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: The long-term outlook for Commanders linebacker Frankie Luvu is good. What does that mean for Sunday's game at Dallas?
articles.body:
Washington Commanders linebacker Frankie Luvu entered the 2026 season in a contract year. After a dominant debut season for the Commanders in 2024, Luvu struggled last season and was often forced to play out of position out of necessity.

When new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones took over, he couldn't hide his excitement to coach Luvu. Instead of playing primarily as an edge rusher or dropping into coverage, Jones planned to use Luvu where he excelled. In Washington's Week 1 game against the Philadelphia Eagles , Luvu had four tackles, including a tackle for loss and a sack. Unfortunately, he departed in the third quarter with an injury and did not return.

Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that Luvu has a groin injury, but didn't offer a timeline for his return.

"So, the four of them, Frankie had a groin, and Chig (Okonkwo) and Jordan (Magee) both had hamstrings, and Tyler (Owens) had an ankle," Quinn said. "I'll have a better update Wednesday as to where they're at. For the soft-tissue ones, we'll need a day or two more with that."

Luvu, along with Okonkwo and Magee, are dealing with soft-tissue injuries, which means they could at least miss the Week 2 game at Dallas .

ESPN NFL insider Jeremy Fowler provided an update on Luvu, and it's good news for Washington.

No trip to IR means that Washington expects him to be out only a short time. However, that doesn't mean he'll play on Sunday against the Cowboys. Fowler's report echoes what Quinn said. If Luvu misses Sunday's game, the Commanders have Sonny Styles and Leo Chenal available to play inside. If Magee can't go, that seriously hampers Washington's depth, leaving Kain Medrano as the only other healthy linebacker on the roster behind Styles and Chenal.

So, good news and bad news on Luvu. Washington will take this, though, as Luvu is an important part of its defense. The Cowboys will need all hands on deck against the Cowboys on Sunday. Dallas, like Washington, is looking to avoid a 0-2 start with two division losses to begin the season.

articles.title: Wolff: “Russell’s Potential Is There, We Just Have to Unlock It”
articles.summary: The Mercedes director admits that the Briton is going through a psychological slump after losing ground to Antonelli. He acknowledges his undeniable quality...
articles.body:
Toto Wolffhas put the focus on the human factor. The Mercedes director, aware of thedifficult situation George Russell is going through in the championship fight,has admitted that the team must work to help the Briton recover his bestversion. After the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid, where Kimi Antonellionce again beat him and extended his advantage to 81 points, Wolff reflected onthe challenges his driver faces.

"You can see the pace he had toward the end, when hewas catching Leclerc, you know he was the fastest on track but after the tirechanges, the pace wasn't there and I just don't know where it is, we have toanalyze it because it's clearly in him, it's in the car and we just have tounlock it" declared Wolff after the race.

Russell 's weekend at Madring was complicated from the start.The Briton openly admitted his problems with tire degradation that preventedhim from fighting for pole position and relegated him to sixth position inqualifying. In the race, the team opted for a two stop strategy, switchingRussell to medium tires under the Virtual Safety Car and returning to the hardslater, although the driver initially questioned the decision, he lateracknowledged that it did not significantly affect his final fifth place result.

Wolff did not hold back on praise for Russell's trajectory,recalling his achievements before arriving in Formula 1: "When it comesto George, you can have good races, bad races, good years and bad years but weare talking about the driver who has won everything you could potentially havewon. Every karting championship, Formula 3 in his rookie year, Formula 2 in hisrookie year, then Williams, we are talking about a top level driver" he stated.

The Mercedes director acknowledged that the psychologicalaspect plays a fundamental role in this situation: "We need to discoverwhat he needs to unlock that potential and of course there is the psychologicalside. If you have a streak like his this year, you are taking hits but thegreat ones recover and I think George has everything he needs to fight forchampionships" explained Wolff.

Despite Antonelli's advantage, Wolff refused to consider thetitle fight over: "It's a mechanical sport, you can retire, you cancrash and it happens twice in a row and suddenly what seemed like a goodcushion is no longer there because there are six races left. In my opinion, wejust need to ignore the points until it is mathematically unrealistic or notreal, that they can win. Until then concentrate on every weekend and try to doour best" he pointed out.

Wolff also revealed that the development of the 2027 car hasbeen underway since before the summer: "2027 started a while ago forus, long before the summer. We shifted resources toward next year and thatcontinues according to plan, regardless of where we are in thechampionship" he concluded.

Mercedes looks to the future without losing sight of thepresent, aware that the key to success lies in recovering a Russell who stillhas a lot to prove.

articles.title: Joe Bowen Reacts as Maple Leafs Make Broadcast Changes for 2026-27 Official
articles.summary: Joe Bowen reacts as the Maple Leafs name Todd Crocker his successor, while his son, David Bowen, joins the Marlies broadcast team. The post Joe Bowen Reacts...
articles.body:
Joe Bowen shared his reaction after the Toronto Maple Leafs officially named Todd Crocker as his successor. That was not the only move announced by the organization. Bowen's son, David was named one of the play-by-play announcers for the Toronto Marlies.

Crocker, a longtime Toronto Marlies announcer, will take over the mic after Bowen retired last season. He spent the past 13 seasons calling Marlies games and will be the Maple Leafs' new radio voice alongside Jim Ralph. He faces a tough task, as he follows Bowen, who served as the Leafs' voice for 44 years.

Bowen extended a congratulatory message as Crocker begins the next chapter of his broadcasting career. He also shared his heartfelt congratulations to his son, who officially joins the organization.

Joe Bowen Reacts as Maple Leafs Name Todd Crocker as His Successor

Joe Bowen is proof that hard work and getting reps in as a broadcaster pay off.

The longtime voice of the Maple Leafs spent years calling OHL games before getting his big break with Toronto. He would go on to have a legendary broadcast career as the voice of the Leafs and is beloved by the fanbase. The organization celebrated him throughout last season, which marked his final year on the mic.

Now, Todd Crocker steps into that role and aims to bring his own style to the booth. Bowen congratulated the longtime Marlies announcer for earning the role and noted that he will be in good hands.

"Wishing Todd all the best. He will enjoy sitting beside my longtime partner Jim Ralph," Bowen posted on X .

Ralph developed great chemistry with Bowen during their time as broadcast partners, so Crocker will be alongside an experienced NHL color commentator.

Bowen Reacts to His Son Joining the Marlies' Broadcast Team

Bowen also shifted his attention to his son, David, who earned a big career move of his own. David Bowen was officially named as one of three Marlies play-by-play announcers for the 2026-27 AHL season.

Bowen, 25, notably filled in for his father on 'Holy Mackinaw! Night' last season, when the organization celebrated his father's career. The game was a full-circle moment as he followed his father's footsteps and called a Leafs game alongside Ralph.

The former voice of the Leafs expressed joy and wished his son well as he succeeds Crocker.

"What a great opportunity for @bonsie34 to get his foot in the door with the @TorontoMarlies as play-by-play broadcaster," Bowen wrote on X . "Dad is over the moon about the opportunity. Big shoes to fill in for @ToddCrocker."

Bowen's son also shared his reaction to joining the Marlies broadcast team this season.

"It's an honor to join the Toronto Marlies as the team's lead play-by-play broadcaster," Bowen said in a press release . "The Marlies have a proud history and an incredibly passionate fan base, and I'm excited to have the opportunity to tell the stories of this team and its players throughout the season. I'm looking forward to working alongside the organization and bringing Marlies hockey to fans across the region and beyond."

Not only will David call Marlies games, but he will also continue calling games for the OHL's Sudbury Wolves.

articles.title: Dayton Dragons season ends losing to Quad Cities in Midwest League Championship Series
articles.summary: The Dayton Dragons’ postseason run ended on Tuesday in a 2-1 loss to Quad City.
articles.body:
The Dayton Dragons' postseason run ended on Tuesday.

The Dragons lost to the Quad Cities River Bandits, 2-1, in Game 2 of the Midwest League Championship Series at Day Air Ballpark.

Blake Mitchell hit a two-run home run with two outs in the eighth inning, giving the River Bandits the lead for good.

Quad Cities wins its ninth Midwest League Championship.

The game was scoreless until the seventh inning. Damian Ruiz hit a triple to left-center, and Kyle Henley followed with an RBI double to give the Dragons a 1-0 lead.

In the top of the eighth, the River Bandits had a runner on third base with two outs. Mitchell hit a home run to right field as Quad Cities took a 2-1 lead.

The Dragons had a runner on second with two outs in the bottom of the eighth, but Johnny Ascanio grounded to second to end the inning.

Dayton ended the regular season with a 67-63 record. They went 39-27 in the first half of the season, clinching the First Half East Division title.

The Dragons advanced to their first-ever Midwest League Championship Series.

They are one of three teams in the county to draw 500,000 fans at home this season.

articles.title: Santos' historic debut in 1912
articles.summary: By Gabriel Pierin, from the Memory CenterThe historic clash brought together Santos Foot-ball Club and its namesake, Santos Athletic Club — today renowned as...
articles.body:
By Gabriel Pierin, from the Memory Center

The historic clash brought together Santos Foot-ball Club and its namesake, Santos Athletic Club — today renowned as the "Englishmen's Club" — at Velo Santista, the former ground of SC Internacional.

On that distant September 15 , 1912, under a radiant Sunday sun, the young left winger Arnaldo Silveira, "Miúdo," just 18 years old, scored the first goal for the fledgling team. The club, which at the time had its headquarters at Largo do Rosário, originally wore white and blue with gold trim.

That first official match of the squad led by Sizino Colatino Martins Patusca served as a prelude to the many decades of glory and major achievements the newly founded club would go on to enjoy.

Santos, which used to train in Villa Macuco, near the Santos docks, lined up for that pioneering match with French goalkeeper Julien Fauvel, Sidnei and Arantes; Ernani, Oscar and Montenegro; Adolpho Millon, Hugo, Nilo, Simon and Arnaldo Silveira.

On the other side, the team from the José Menino neighborhood featured Parsons, Kent and Deweck; Woodon, Seddon and Lee; Saul, De Saone, Allen, V. Cross and Harold Cross. Curiously, one of Santos Athletic's forwards was Harold Cross, one of Santos's own founders, who in the very next fixtures would join Santos's attacking line.

The inaugural encounter ended 3–2 to Santos FBC. The winning goals were scored by Arnaldo Silveira (2) and Adolpho Millon (1), while Lee scored twice for the British side.

On that same pitch, set on the charming and well-known Ana Costa Avenue, Santos played 14 matches, recording 11 wins and three draws, and also won the 1913 Campeonato Santista on that ground .

The press of the time immortalized the event with the following account:

"With a crowd the like of which we had not seen for some time, yesterday's match between the distinguished English Club and Santos Foot-Ball Club took place. Around the field stood the most distinguished English and Brazilian families. There was much discussion over who would win, some favoring the Brazilians, others the English. Once the contest began, at 2:30, the kick-off fell to the nationals, who soon lost the ball, though before long they struck back, putting the English goal in serious danger. After a hard-fought battle, the first half ended with the following result: Santos Athletic Club 1 goal. Santos Foot-Ball Club 1 goal.

In the second half the struggle became fiercer still, and then the fine play of Montenegro, Oscar and Belmarço was seen, increasing the score with 2 more goals for their team. The English, for their part, redoubled their efforts, managing another goal, scored by Lee. It is worth highlighting goalkeeper Fauvel, who played admirably, as well as Montenegro, Simon, Belmarço and Arantes. Among the English, their goalkeeper Person, Lee and Cross stood out. At 3:30 the game ended with the victory of Santos Foot-Ball Club by 3 goals to 2."

That afternoon, with the gates open to the public, Santos's players took the field wearing white long-sleeved dress shirts, with a blue ribbon on their arms.

Adolpho Millon Jr., son of captain Adolpho, and Arnaldo Silveira, nephew of president Sizino Patusca, emerged as the first two idols in the history of the Alvinegro Praiano. Both Meninos da Vila played a decisive role throughout the club's first decade.

The brilliance of the duo up front opened the way for them to be called up as starters for the first Brazilian National Team in history, which played in the 1914 Copa Roca in Argentina. Their partnership with the national team lasted until the 1919 South American Championship, when they became champions wearing Brazil's colors.

Right winger Millon wore Santos's black-and-white shirt until 1922, making 118 appearances and scoring 52 goals. Right winger Arnaldo Silveira, meanwhile, represented the Vila Belmiro eleven 132 times, finding the net on 74 occasions.

Both stand out among the select group of the 39 founders of the most famous black-and-white club in the world.

articles.title: Liverpool agree midfield transfer, and write history for the first time in 100 years
articles.summary: Liverpool have agreed a transfer for an exciting midfielder and wrote history in the process. The midfield is probably the biggest headache for Andoni Iraola...
articles.body:
Liverpool have agreed a transfer for an exciting midfielder and wrote history in the process.

The midfield is probably the biggest headache for Andoni Iraola right now.

It just doesn't feel like he has the right profiles to make his system work as effectively as he wants. At Bournemouth , Iraola had midfielders who could receive the ball and move it on quickly, helping his side transition from defence into attack.

The problems aren't just with what happens when they have possession, either. The midfield looks far too porous, with gaps appearing far too easily and opponents finding space to attack.

That ultimately makes the whole team less effective.

Something has to change. Either Liverpool's current midfielders step up and start delivering the performances Iraola needs, or the Spaniard will have to make some difficult decisions.

The easy solution to Liverpool's midfield problems

Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch are both at their best when carrying the ball, while neither is particularly strong when it comes to winning possession back.

That makes playing the pair together in a double pivot a strange decision.

Alexis Mac Allister looks far better suited to the system and has also started the season in excellent form. Trey Nyoni 's ability on the ball could also make him a really interesting option.

But if Liverpool want an intense ball-winner who can also play out from deep and help build attacks, they may need to look towards the transfer market.

Lamine Camara is reportedly high on the club's shortlist, and a move for the midfielder would make plenty of sense. He could be exactly what Liverpool's midfield is missing.

A new midfielder is coming as Liverpool write history

The Reds did sign a midfielder in the end.

Even though the transfer window shut two weeks ago, Liverpool quietly confirmed the arrival of Patrik Farkas as a free agent on the club's official website.

Farkas has returned to the club after leaving at U16 level to join Blackburn.

He joins his brother Erik, who is expected to sign a professional contract with the club and plays for the Reds' U18 side at the moment.

Together the duo have written history. They have become the first brother duo to represent Liverpool in over 100 years.

Previously, John and Tom Miller represented Liverpool in the 1910s, and early 1920s. Elisha and Billy Scott was another brother duo of the era who played for the Reds.

And now the Farkas brothers have joined the Millers and the Scotts and written themselves in the history books, too.

articles.title: Alex Peixeiro seals Santos win in Cascavel
articles.summary: Santos had a weekend of victories both on the field and on the track. Last Sunday (13), driver Alex Peixeiro, who represents Santos FC in Fórmula Truck, fini...
articles.body:
Santos had a weekend of victories both on the field and on the track. Last Sunday (13), driver Alex Peixeiro, who represents Santos FC in Fórmula Truck, finished in first place in the 7th round of the competition at the Cascavel International Raceway, in Paraná.

Previously, Alex had already reached the podium in other races this season, and now he makes his mark by securing his first victory.

In a weekend full of challenges on the track, the Santos driver had to start from 17th on the grid and fight his way back through the field. "We made several changes and, thank God, they worked very well. So by the end of the weekend, the truck was practically perfect. We're very happy that this was our first win. We already had trophies for second, third, fourth, fifth and sixth place, and first place was the one we were missing," Alex said.

Santos fans were also there to show their support. Held in Paraná, the round drew several supporters to the stands cheering for the black-and-white driver.

"We're creating a culture of fans going to the racetracks wearing Santos shirts. We've already done campaigns, giveaway draws, raffles with my products and with Santos FC products. We want to do more, in a cultural way. And we're planting that seed. These fans are amazing, and it's really great to see Santos supporters sharing the same passion," he added.

The 8th round of Fórmula Truck will take place on October 9, 10 and 11 in Tarumã, Rio Grande do Sul.

articles.title: Arch Manning’s apology leads to Holly Rowe forgiving Texas QB after press conference comments
articles.summary: Texas Longhorns QB Arch Manning found himself in hot water after laughing at an AI video of coach Steve Sarkisian slapping veteran reporter Holly Rowe. The L...
articles.body:
Texas Longhorns QB Arch Manning found himself in hot water after laughing at an AI video of coach Steve Sarkisian slapping veteran reporter Holly Rowe.

The Longhorns' incredible comeback 24-23 win over Ohio State was overshadowed by Sarkisian brushing off Rowe and ending his post-game interview early.

The fallout from that incident led to Texas fans making an AI video of Sarkisian slapping Rowe to end the conversation instead, something Manning found amusing, and now regrets.

Holly Rowe accepts Arch Manning's apology after private conversation

Rowe put an end to the backlash against Manning for his insensitive reaction to the AI video at a press conference by publicly forgiving the 22-year-old after a private conversation.

"Thank you, Arch. I appreciate our conversation about this, which will remain private. Apology accepted. We move forward with respect and kindness for one another."

Manning shared his apology on social media, accepting the lapse in his judgment, taking accountability for his hurtful reaction to the video, and apologising to Rowe.

"In my press conference yesterday, I made an insensitive comment about an AI video. There is nothing funny about it. It's easy to say I didn't mean it, but I know my words and actions were hurtful to a lot of people. I do not take that lightly and am deeply sorry for that."

"I specifically want to apologize to Holly Rowe for what she has personally had to deal with because of my comments. I have a ton of respect for her and appreciate her showing me grace in this moment. I need to do better and will be more thoughtful going forward."

What did Arch Manning say about Holly Rowe?

Manning was asked about the Sarkisian-Rowe exchange after the win over Ole Miss in a press conference on September 14, where he laughed about an AI video where Sarkisian slaps Rowe.

"I have seen a few AI edits of Sark earlier. Have you seen that one? Of him slapping Holly Rowe? It's hilarious."

The backlash to this comment was bigger than what Sarkisian received for brushing off Rowe as a whole, further magnifying an already inflamed incident between the coach and the reporter.

articles.title: Why Ben Johnson was a little disappointed with Chicago Bears’ 59-37 Week 1 win
articles.summary: Ben Johnson spoke about the Chicago Bears’ dominant 59-37 win against the Carolina Panthers, and why he didn’t feel thrilled with the result. The Bears looke...
articles.body:
Ben Johnson spoke about the Chicago Bears ' dominant 59-37 win against the Carolina Panthers , and why he didn't feel thrilled with the result.

The Bears looked incredible against the Panthers, with Caleb Williams in particular delivering a sensational performance.

But Ben Johnson couldn't help but feel that the Bears left something on the table in the win, even if it was just by a very small margin.

Ben Johnson wanted Chicago Bears to score 60+ points against Carolina Panthers

When speaking with Jeff Joniak of ESPN Chicago radio, Ben Johnson had a very simple response when the veteran broadcaster admitted he was hoping the Chicago Bears would score 60+ points.

Johnson admitted that he also wanted the Bears to cross the 60-point mark during the game, but they missed it by just one point.

Jeff Joniak: "At that point I was hoping for 60! I was thinking of a two-point try at some point."

Ben Johnson: "I don't think you were the only one (hoping for 60 points)…"

Even with the Bears failing to score 60+ points against the Panthers, there is no denying just how well they played in Week 1.

It was a statement performance from the team, who were eager to prove that their performances last season were no fluke.

Williams had a stellar night, throwing for 269 yards with two touchdowns across 29 attempted passes, while carrying for two more touchdowns with 65 rushing yards.

Many have predicted that Williams will be an MVP contender, and his first performance did little to dissuade this notion.

If there was any criticism to be had, it could be for the Bears' defense for letting the Panthers score 37 points against them.

The Panthers are far from the most potent offensive team in the NFL, so letting them score as frequently as the Bears did isn't exactly a good look.

Hopefully, as the season goes on, Johnson and the coaching staff can ensure that the defensive unit improves.

articles.title: Report: Klopp set to leave Undav out of Germany squad
articles.summary: New Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is set to leave VfB Stuttgart striker Deniz Undav out of his squad for the upcoming Nations League matches, broadcaster Sky ha...
articles.body:
New Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is set to leave VfB Stuttgart striker Deniz Undav out of his squad for the upcoming Nations League matches, broadcaster Sky have reported.

Undav has already been told in a personal conversation with Klopp that he will not be included in the squad, according to Tuesday night's report.

The 30-year-old is a key player for Stuttgart and their new captain but has yet to score this season. He has, however, provided four assists in all competitions.

Undav has an impressive record for Germany, scoring nine goals in just 13 international appearances.

He also scored three times at the World Cup earlier this year under Klopp's predecessor Julian Nagelsmann, with all three goals coming as a substitute. Before Germany's opening game against Curaçao , Klopp had said he would have liked to have seen Undav in the starting line-up.

Klopp is instead expected to turn to Eintracht Frankfurt forwards Younes Ebnoutalib and Jonathan Burkardt when he names his squad on Thursday, according to media reports.

Ebnoutalib would be making his Germany debut. The striker is also eligible to represent Morocco .

Germany play their first matches under Klopp away to the Netherlands on September 24, at home to Greece on September 27 and Serbia on October 1, before travelling to Greece on October 4.

Klopp is due to announce his squad on Thursday.

articles.title: Knicks reportedly sign $21M 7-year high-motor veteran to pair with Jalen Brunson, OG Anunoby
articles.summary: The New York Knicks are looking to win back to back championships. They just agreed to a deal with the top free agent, bolstering their roster.
articles.body:
The past few weeks for John Konchar have been wild, to say the least, as he has been involved in some crazy whirlwinds of roster moves. He is one of the top free agents available after being released by the Minnesota Timberwolves .

"The Minnesota Timberwolves have traded Josh Green and cash to the Utah Jazz for Cody Williams and John Konchar, the teams announced Saturday. The Timberwolves are expected to keep Williams, the No. 10 pick in 2024, and waive-and-stretch Konchar, sources told ESPN. Saturday is the final day to waive a player and stretch out his guaranteed salary over multiple seasons," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote.

As one of the top free agents left with training camp approaching, Konchar had multiple teams interested in him. The New York Knicks , Toronto Raptors , and Miami Heat were among the teams to show interest.

"John Konchar is one of the top free agents available and has drawn interest, league sources say, from Miami, New York, Orlando and Toronto," The Stein Line's Marc Stein wrote.

On Tuesday night, Konchar's agent let ESPN's Shams Charania know that his client would be signing with New York.

"Free agent forward John Konchar agreed to a deal with the New York Knicks , agent George S. Langberg of GSL Sports Group told ESPN on Tuesday night. Konchar, 30, is entering his eighth NBA season after spending 2025-26 with the Utah Jazz and Memphis Grizzlies ," Charania wrote.

This is a huge addition for the Knicks, as they get a reliable veteran who will provide great depth. Konchar will be able to step up when guys miss games, which will happen at some point.

Konchar has made $21 million in his career to this point. It is still unknown what the exact deal is until it is finalized. However, it seems like New York got one of the guys they have been so patient to wait on.

articles.title: Devils Sign Luke Evangelista to 5-Year, $36.25M ($7.25M AAV) Contract Extension
articles.summary: Two weeks after acquiring Evangelista from Nashville, Sunny Mehta secured his services for the next half decade.
articles.body:
When the Devils acquired winger Luke Evangelista a few weeks ago, one of the first questions that I asked was whether or not the Devils should sign him to a contract extension.

If you've been paying attention to what's going on around the league, there has been a flurry of contract extensions across the NHL. Yesterday was the last day for teams to sign players for a maximum of eight years, and we saw a few of those deals with Drake Batherson extending in Ottawa , Noah Ostlund in Buffalo, and Ryan Leonard and Justin Sourdif in Washington DC. So it was fair to wonder if any of the Devils pending free agents would put pen to paper, as Jackson wrote about earlier this week .

Sunny Mehta didn't quite go the full eight years of term with Evangelista, but late Tuesday night, he did get Evangelista to agree to terms on a new five year contract. The deal is for $36.25M total ($7.25M AAV). The deal will begin with the 2027-28 season and will be tacked on to the final year of his current $3M AAV deal.

The contract breakdown is as follows: 2027-28: $9,700,000; 2028-29: $8,260,000; 2029-30: $6,120,000; 2030-31: $6,085,000 & 2031-32: $6,085,000.

According to PuckPedia, the deal is signing bonus heavy, with roughly 75% of it coming in bonuses ($27.915M). There is also relatively light trade protection over the final three years of the deal with a 7-team no-trade list in 2029-30, a five team no-trade list in 2030-31, and a three team list in 2031-32. The deal is also buying out three years of UFA.

My initial reaction was that it seems a little high given some of the recent comparables. Evangelista secures a bigger AAV than Fraser Minten (7x$7.2M) who really just has the one full NHL season to speak of and plays a premium position. He comes in higher than Connor McMichael (6x$6.75M), although he does have a higher scoring rate for his career.

After taking a step back though and looking at it again, I think it's just where the NHL is going nowadays and getting a top six winger under $10M is probably a bargain at this rate. Especially when you're buying out three years of unrestricted free agency beginning in 2029-30.

We're seeing more and more teams make those long-term bets on their young players that they envision being part of their core. When your options are sign the player now or pay more for the same player a year from now, I get why teams are being proactive when it comes to signing their own. The salary cap is only continuing to increase and yesterday's price isn't today's price.

Evangelista has 253 games of NHL experience, so it's not a pure gamble like, say, what the Sabres are doing with Ostlund and his 68 games of experience. Granted, we don't know how he's going to fit in yet with THIS Devils team since he has yet to play a game for the Devils. But if he fits in well, that contract would've only gotten more expensive next summer if he put up another 56 point season playing out his current deal.

I view this bet as being similar to the ones that Mehta (or more specifically, Bill Zito) made in Florida with players such as Carter Verhaeghe , Sam Bennett , Sam Reinhart , and others. Florida was proactive in getting their supporting cast locked up on manageable deals and it paid off in a big way on the back end of those deals when those players became key contributors on their Stanley Cup championship teams. I also look at the market in general and acknowledge that UFA isn't going to be the answer. Especially when players like the aforementioned Batherson remove themselves from the equation by forgoing UFA and signing long-term in Ottawa.

At the end of the day, I'm not surprised that Mehta doubled down on the bet he previously made by acquiring Evangelista in the first place. This deal only reaffirms his belief in said player.

That's how I'm looking at this deal. Perhaps you are looking at it differently. Please feel free to leave a comment below, and thanks for reading.
