articles.title: 'He's an idiot, but he's our idiot' - Saints fans on Pollock contract stand-off
articles.summary: How has a drawn-out and public contract negotiation affected the relationship between Henry Pollock and his fans?
articles.body:
Henry Pollock is determined not to blink first in his contractual face-off.

Despite a deal with Northampton being close, amid reports of an agreement of about £400,000 a year, the back row stressed on Monday that his renewal was not signed.

Asked if he was looking forward to the end of the saga, stoked by Pollock's advisor Eddie Hearn, Saints director of rugby Phil Dowson joked that "it would have been good to have it sorted three weeks ago".

The haggling has certainly played out more publicly than most negotiations.

Has it taken some of the sheen off a player who was key to Saints winning the Prem title last season and whose public profile has brought new supporters and attention, not just to his club but to his sport in general?

'The theatre around it will grind people's gears'

Lis Saunders is the chair of the Northampton Saints Supporters Group.

"I have known Henry coming up through the academy and he is absolutely delightful," she told BBC Sport.

"The perception of his arrogance is wrong. He is just a young bouncy man, living his best life.

"Some people are getting a bit fed up with the whole theatre around [the contract stand-off], though.

"I am laissez-faire about it. If he stays it will be brilliant, but you can't keep someone who wants to go.

"The whole theatre around it is what will grind people's gears. You are starting to see that on some of the fan forums – people saying, 'Either sign or don't. Just don't mess around - we don't need this drama.'"

Saunders points out that, while Pollock can pull a crowd, Saints invariably fill Franklin's Gardens anyway. The turnstiles will carry on clicking at the same rate regardless of his presence.

It would be an emotional wrench rather than a financial loss if he moves elsewhere.

"As the players themselves say, he's an idiot, but he's our idiot," said Saunders.

"We've watched him grow up and he's very much ours. It would be really sad if he didn't stay - perhaps understandable, but really sad."

Charles McGillivray is one of the hosts of Beneath the Lift Tower, a Northampton Saints podcast run by fans and named after the landmark that looms over Franklin's Gardens.

He says the stand-off has split fans, even if Pollock, who was superb at the end of last season, still has the support of the majority.

"There are probably two ends of the spectrum," he said.

"You've got some fans who are just reading headlines, may not be as engaged as others and don't really understand the mechanics of how rugby clubs in England work, with the salary cap and things like that.

"But most Saints fans are fairly grounded. They understand that Eddie Hearn coming to Henry Pollock's career is going to be brilliant for the sport and together they're going to make lots of noise.

"And they also understand that the money being quoted [Hearn says Pollock is worth £1m a season] isn't really feasible to be earned by someone in England.

"We think he's a grounded - if ambitious - lad and therefore Northampton is the best place for him to be.

"There isn't a club in England at the moment developing talent at the rate of knots or to the level that Northampton is. And maybe only Bath are having the continued success that Northampton are having."

McGillivray's co-host Simon Stacey, who has been following the club for 40 years, points out that Northampton fans have seen first hand the risks that players run for their rewards.

In 2018 Saints centre Rob Horne went in for a hard but routine tackle and incurred nerve damage that cost him the use of his right arm.

"I don't hold any grudges against Henry," said Stacey. "It doesn't annoy me. I get that they do need to get what they can because it's a short career and they have to look after themselves."

With a club's spending on salaries capped at £6.4m - with another £1.4m available in various credits and compensations - a bumper pay deal for one player at a Prem club reduces the money available for others.

Last autumn scrum-half Alex Mitchell said he and others had prioritised the togetherness and quality of Saints' squad over "mega money" elsewhere when opting to re-sign.

While Northampton did not pay up to the salary cap in the most recent report on Prem club finances, which covers the 2024-25 season, a raft of renewals is likely to take them closer to the limit in the coming years.

However, if Pollock's stance is causing ructions in the squad, they are hiding it well.

Fly-half Fin Smith momentarily joined Hearn in lobbying for Pollock to be granted a £1m annual salary this month, telling reporters that "he's worth it" before joking that Pollock had sent him out to do a bit of PR on his behalf.

Dowson dropped a request into the squad's group chat, asking if the squad could borrow the private jet Hearn had laid on for Pollock to visit him on the French Rivera.

As Pollock gave an interview on Monday, soberly stressing that the forthcoming season could be his last at the club, his straight face briefly broke as Mitchell smirked at him from across the room.

Hearn has said he found Pollock's current earnings at Northampton, thought to be about £150,000 a year, to be unbelievable. And not in a good way.

Certainly, Pollock, one of the faces of the sport, is due a significant pay raise.

The league's latest salary cap report is revealing.

His current salary is below that of the 2024-25 league average of £191,000.

Of the players in his current age bracket (20-22) that season, 27% were paid more than he is now.

Pollock has 13 England caps. The average wage of a player with 11-20 caps was £224,000.

Even if he finalises his reported extension, it will be at a lower level than the average 'marquee' player – those whose pay is excluded from the salary cap – took home in 2024-25. That figure was £533,000.

Finn Russell, the Scotland fly-half and only other rugby player who is part of Hearn's Matchroom stable, is one of those marquee players, on a deal worth about £1m a year with Bath.

Pollock has long since outgrown his current deal, signed in December 2024 before his England debut, Champions Cup knockout heroics and British and Irish Lions call-up.

The obvious destination were Pollock to move within the Prem.

Backed by Austrian energy drink dynasty, Pollock would be a statement signing that fits their youth-orientated brand. The club had plenty of headroom on the pay roll, spending barely half of the salary cap's upper limit in 2024-25 campaign.

However, a revamp of the playing squad since then will have given them less ability to manoeuvre, and Prem Rugby rules on domestic moves prevent Pollock from being the club's designated marquee player for his first two seasons elsewhere.

Pollock would also have to weigh up whether swapping the Prem champions for the league's bottom club, who are without Champions Cup rugby for 2026-27 at least, is desirable.

French clubs operate under a significantly higher salary cap of 11m euros (£9.4m), and the Top14 is booming, challenging football for prominence in the country.

Thanks to skirmishes with Bordeaux-Begles in the Champions Cup, Pollock has pantomime villain status in the country.

He was jeered the loudest of any player when England played France in Paris in March. His vigorous celebrations of Tommy Freeman's 76th-minute try, which appeared to have clinched the win for the visitors, will have further endeared him to the locals.

However, a move across the Channel would come at the cost of Pollock's England career and the associated central contract, worth about £150,000.

There is also a considerable cultural shock to overcome. Courtney Lawes, a Northampton legend, has just returned to England, saying some aspects of his two-season spell with Brive were challenging.

Henry Arundell, the bright, young thing of English rugby before Pollock, endured a difficult time at Racing 92 before returning to the Prem a year earlier than anticipated.

The money-making move of choice for many of the southern hemisphere's finest.

Richie Mo'unga, Pieter Steph du Toit and Malcolm Marx are among those who have enjoyed the lighter schedule and yen-heavy pay days in Japan.

While England internationals George Kruis and Alex Goode have made moves there in the past, there has been a shift lately to favour Japanese players over big-money imports.

Both Kruis and Goode were near the end of their careers. A switch to such relative obscurity would do little to build Pollock's brand in rugby's major markets.

Perhaps the most intriguing comment made by Pollock this week was a desire to explore "other sports" during his career.

He has been a ringside regular since signing with Matchroom, most recently attending Katie Taylor's farewell fight at Dublin's Croke Park, and chatting with UFC fighter Ian Machado Garry at a recent charity fundraising event.

His high-energy style would suit a switch to rugby league, and it has been reported that a number of Super League clubs, buoyed by possible investment from the NRL, are monitoring Pollock's situation.

The big-money start-up circuit, originally slated to begin next month, would surely have been keen on Pollock.

However, it has been postponed until 2028 and, with conflict in the Middle East further unsettling investors and logistics, looks increasingly unlikely to transpire.

articles.title: Brewers' Pat Murphy talks clinching the NL Central wearing comically large goggles
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers are one of the best feel-good stories in sports, but they are certainly not a plucky underdog. This franchise is a Goliath disguised as...
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are one of the best feel-good stories in sports, but they are certainly not a plucky underdog. This franchise is a Goliath disguised as a David. Sure, there are no championships to celebrate, at least not yet, but stacking 90-win campaigns with a bottom-half payroll and young roster is borderline miraculous. Many people have become numb to the Brew Crew's greatness, especially after they clinched their fourth consecutive National League Central title on Tuesday, but this run of consistent excellence deserves thorough appreciation.

Pat Murphy understands the magnitude of what his team is accomplishing. He reflected on it while wearing a massive pair of goggles on his head.

"We have 11 games to go, a lot of things to tighten up, but it's just really gratifying to see the guys know what they've achieved and know that it's never been done four years in a row," the two-time reigning NL Manager of the Year said while taking a break from the champagne shower, per the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel's Todd Rosiak. "I'm just happy for them."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Brewers (94-57) fittingly retained their divisional crown on the night that NL Cy Young favorite and flame-throwing phenom Jacob Misiorowski pitched. He threw five shutout innings, Joey Ortiz notched three hits and two RBIs and the team grabbed a 5-1 road win versus the Pittsburgh Pirates . They still needed some help, though. The Chicago Cubs once again staggered in the later innings and suffered a 6-3 home loss against the Atlanta Braves . Cream City would not want it any other way.

Milwaukee has reached the point where only a World Series appearance will feel like a genuine success, and that in itself is truly remarkable. The Los Angeles Dodgers are deeper than anyone on paper, but the Brewers continue to prove that evaluating teams on paper can be a deeply flawed methodology.

Outlasting LA and a fierce NL playoff field could be extremely challenging. The baseball gods have punished this franchise many times, often in cruel fashion. Eventually, though, regular season domination should yield October euphoria.

The two-time defending champion Dodgers are chasing a rare feat, but so is this group. The Brewers have waited almost 60 years to experience the ultimate celebration, and in what will likely be a record-setting year for the organization, perhaps their time will finally come.

Milwaukee deserves recognition regardless, but a World Series victory may be the only way to receive proper acknowledgement for its cumulative success.

articles.title: Northeast High School students go wild as Jalen Hurts announces $600K donation in viral video
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts is keeping things cool off the field, for some very excited students in high school. As a Super Bowl champion and Super Bowl MVP with the Philade...
articles.body:
Jalen Hurts is keeping things cool off the field, for some very excited students in high school.

As a Super Bowl champion and Super Bowl MVP with the Philadelphia Eagles, Jalen Hurts is a bona fide legend to every sports fan in Philly.

The quarterback has already provided fans with some of their happiest moments, but he is now motivated to do the same off the court.

And following one of his recent charitable donations, the reactions Hurts got from the students he was offering to help has gone viral online.

Watch Jalen Hurts announce massive donation to high school for ACs

Hurts is using his foundation to donate $600,000 to the Northeast High School in Rhawnhurst, Philadelphia, so that they can get air conditioning.

The QB showed up at a school event on Tuesday to announce the donation, much to the delight of the students in attendance. A video of it went viral, with Hurts also explaining why he decided to help with this issue.

"I can imagine that you guys would like ACs and a little bit of fresh air, too," Hurts told the cheering throng of students.

He later explained his donation, saying, "Watching the morning news, in the fall on an off day. Being from the South, I was very blown away by school being cancelled.

"Not for snow, not for a hurricane, not for a tropical storm. But for a lack of AC. It's a common thing I didn't necessarily think about… So that's something I wanna pay for."

This is a move that will win over the hearts of even more people in Philly. Hurts is quickly turning himself into a hero off the field just as much as he is one on it.

articles.standfirst: El sevillano y el argentino superan en el ranking a Jon Sanz y Franco Stupaczuk tras firmar las semifinales en el Paris Major
articles.summary: El sevillano y el argentino superan en el ranking a Jon Sanz y Franco Stupaczuk tras firmar las semifinales en el Paris Major
articles.body: Paquito Navarro y Martín Di Nenno han alcanzado la cuarta posición del ranking FIP tras su actuación en el Paris Major. La dupla hispano-argentina ha adelantado a Franco Stupaczuk y Jon Sanz —quienes ostentaban dicha condición hasta la fecha—, así como a Mike Yanguas y Coki Nieto, en la pugna por un puesto clave que permite evitar a las dos primeras parejas del cuadro hasta la ronda de semifinales. Desde el inicio de su proyecto conjunto, Navarro y Di Nenno han consolidado una dinámica regular en los torneos de máxima categoría, cosechando cuatro presencias en semifinales desde su unión. Estos resultados, sumados a las eliminaciones tempranas de sus rivales directos en el cuadro parisino, les permiten situarse como cabezas de serie número cuatro, un estatus que ninguno de los dos ocupaba desde la temporada 2024. El desenlace en Roland Garros también ha traído consecuencias en la parte alta de la tabla masculina. Arturo Coello y Agustín Tapia, tras proclamarse campeones, han ampliado su ventaja en el liderato frente a Ale Galán y Fede Chingotto. De haber obtenido el título la pareja número dos, habría asaltado el primer puesto de la Race; sin embargo, el triunfo de Coello y Tapia sitúa la distancia en más de 4.000 puntos en la clasificación general FIP y en 2.500 unidades en la tabla anual. En la zona media, Aimar Goñi y Edu Alonso registran un importante ascenso tras alcanzar los cuartos de final en la capital francesa. El jugador navarro se aproxima al top 30 tras subir cuatro posiciones, mientras que el drive valenciano se sitúa 17º en la Race, a menos de 300 puntos del corte para el Tour Finals que marca Javi Leal. Por su parte, Juani De Pascual firma la progresión más acusada del torneo al escalar diez puestos y colocarse en el lugar 43 del ranking. En el apartado femenino, la consecución del título en la pista Philippe Chatrier por parte de Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero no altera su condición como tercera pareja del ranking, si bien Sánchez asciende dos posiciones en el escalafón individual para colocarse tercera, por delante de Paula Josemaría y Bea González. Pese a caer en semifinales, Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea amplían su colchón en el liderato del ranking FIP. Sánchez y Ustero se mantienen a 3.000 puntos en la clasificación general de Paula y Bea, aunque reducen la brecha en la Race hasta los 800 puntos, en un tramo de curso donde la defensa de puntos del año anterior resultará determinante. En el resto de la tabla, Martina Calvo se sitúa como octava jugadora del mundo, mientras que Claudia Jensen asciende dos plazas para colocarse décima. Respecto al acceso al Master Final, Aranza Osoro reduce distancias con el corte que marca Verónica Virseda, al tiempo que Alejandra Salazar consolida su margen dentro de las posiciones de privilegio. El circuito oficial Premier Padel afronta ahora dos citas consecutivas de categoría P2 en Rotterdam y Düsseldorf, previas al P1 de Milán y al Major de Kuwait programado para finales de octubre.

articles.title: (Video) Liverpool fans will love what Barcola and Gakpo did in reaction to Szoboszlai wonder goal
articles.summary: Dominik Szoboszlai stunned Anfield with a simply spectacular goal in Liverpool’s 3-1 win over Tottenham Hotspur on Tuesday night, and even some of his teamma...
articles.body:
Dominik Szoboszlai stunned Anfield with a simply spectacular goal in Liverpool 's 3-1 win over Tottenham Hotspur on Tuesday night, and even some of his teammates couldn't quite believe what they witnessed.

The Reds were tentatively holding to a one-goal advantage over their visitors going into stoppage time when the Hungarian settled the tie once and for all in show-stopping fashion, crashing a thundering volley from 30 yards past helpless Spurs goalkeeper Martin Dubravka .

The 25-year-old has plenty of previous for long-range goals , but the strike that he produced last night may well have been the best of the lot.

Barcola and Gakpo reactions to Szoboszlai screamer were brilliant

Liverpool's official X channel shared a clip of the Szoboszlai goal an hour after the match, and the reactions of two of his teammates summed up just how spectacular a moment it was.

Cody Gakpo – whose assist for the goal was a piece of artistry as he chipped the ball over Lucas Bergvall – performed a knee slide on the sodden turf inside the penalty area, while Bradley Barcola put his hands in his head in disbelief at what he'd just seen from the Reds' number 8.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Those reactions said it all about how spectacular a goal it was

The instant reactions from the two forwards spoke volumes about the quality of the Hungarian's strike, which added to brilliantly taken goals from Alexis Mac Allister and Gakpo earlier on the night.

Barcola's stunned silence may well have been replicated by plenty of Liverpool fans in the stands and watching at home, while the Dutchman's knee slide was as if he'd just scored himself, although he can rightly take plenty of acclaim for his exquisite assist.

Szoboszlai didn't actually have the best of games prior to that moment, with the 25-year-old losing three of his four duels and giving up possession cheaply at times ( Sofascore ), but he once again showed his ability to come up with a clutch moment in some style.

While we'd still like to see more from him in terms of his overall performance, few players at Anfield can match his propensity to win a game from nowhere with a piece of show-stopping brilliance.

As Andoni Iraola said after the match (via liverpoolfc.com ), 'everyone is thinking he might score' from that range, and they were proven right once more.

Liverpool contract talks continue over Rio Ngumoha amid transfer interest

Fabrizio Romano has confirmed Liverpool are in discussions with Rio Ngumoha over a new contract, with talks ongoing as the club look to secure the future of one of the most highly regarded young talents in their ranks.The situation appears clear from Liverpool's side. Despite recurring noise in the market and continued attention from major clubs, the internal stance has remained firm for some time. Rio Ngumoha is viewed as a player for the future at Anfield, and there has been no willingness to entertain an exit.However, Romano also acknowledged that Premier League rivals Arsenal would be in the mix for the youngster if he was to look to leave Liverpool.

There was significant interest during the summer, with Bayern Munich among the clubs linked, while other sides across Europe were also monitoring developments. Liverpool's message throughout that period was consistent, that the player would not be leaving and was not available for transfer.That position has not shifted. Instead, the focus has moved towards extending his terms and reinforcing his place in the club's long-term project. For Liverpool, this is part of a wider strategy around elite youth retention, particularly when players begin attracting attention from domestic and European rivals.

Arsenal interest could remain in background

Arsenal have also been mentioned in connection with Ngumoha and, as with many leading clubs, they are expected to stay alert to any elite market opportunity. The expectation is that if any opening were to emerge in 2027, 2028, or beyond, Arsenal would be one of several sides keeping a close watch on the situation.For now, though, there is no indication Liverpool are preparing to weaken their position. Quite the opposite, discussions over a new deal suggest they want to strengthen it.

Liverpool transfer strategy around young talent

With Liverpool continuing to plan for the future under Andoni Iraola , locking down premium academy and development talent remains an important part of the club's wider recruitment and squad-building model. Ngumoha is clearly seen within that category.As matters stand, Liverpool are talking contract, not transfer. That distinction is the key point, and one that underlines how strongly the club value Rio Ngumoha.

articles.title: Chiefs news: Travis Kelce drops NSFW philosophy powering Kansas City
articles.summary: Travis Kelce credits Kansas City’s renewed edge to a coach who never left the building in spirit and has now returned to it in practice. Speaking on New Heig...
articles.body:
Travis Kelce credits Kansas City 's renewed edge to a coach who never left the building in spirit and has now returned to it in practice. Speaking on New Heights with his brother Jason, the veteran tight end explained what Eric Bieniemy has brought back to the Chiefs since rejoining as offensive coordinator, and the philosophy behind it is not exactly family-friendly.

"It's a breath of fresh air, man. I think we all know that old ball coach that will tell you that we got to run it down this mother," Kelce said in the podcast . "If you say that every day that we put on pads, you start to create a mentality and a mindset that I have no other option other than run through this mother. So he's told it to me 10 times now."

Kelce's larger point was about the value of repetition. "You start to incorporate that and it starts to become who you are, so that in the fourth quarter of Week 10, when this team has seen this play not only twice this game but 10 other games that you've already played, and they know it's coming because you're in the same formation and you're doing the same motion, you're going to be ready to run it through this mother's face," he said. "That's something that EB has always been unbelievable at."

Bieniemy is back in Kansas City for his second stint as offensive coordinator after holding the role from 2018 to 2022, a run that included two Super Bowl titles and Patrick Mahomes ' first MVP season. He left for Washington in 2023, then spent a year at UCLA and 2025 coaching running backs in Chicago before the Chiefs brought him back to replace Matt Nagy.

The mentality showed up in Week 1. Kansas City ran for 220 yards on 38 carries in its 31-10 rout of the Broncos , with Kenneth Walker III breaking off a 60-yard touchdown in the third quarter. Kelce added a 59-yard catch and run in Mahomes' first game back from ACL and LCL surgery .

The Chiefs host the Colts on Sunday Night Football looking to carry the approach into Week 2.

Following a lengthy legal battle over the last two years, both parties agreed to move the trial from federal court to private arbitration a few months ago. Before that, Janel Grant also spoke about the details of her case in her first-ever public appearance.What shocking confession did Janel Grant make about the lawsuit against Vince McMahon?Janel Grant was awarded the 2026 Advocacy in Action Award from the Connecticut Alliance to End Sexual Violence on September 11. While accepting the honor, Grant made a shocking revelation. She confirmed that she had been tied to an NDA that forbade her from revealing the dark details she endured at the hands of Vince McMahon, according to her allegations. Grant said that it nearly took her life and damaged every part of her life.Grant said, "Around six weeks ago, that life saved was mine. And what you’re witnessing right now is one giant miracle because it’s taken a village of people and a collective effort to keep me alive and get me here today, like a continued day-to-day effort," said Grant. The power of an NDA nearly took my life, took my life. What I’ve survived is one, two, three, four years of across-the-board life wreck, like physical health, mental health, my, oh goodness, my support system, my safety, my security, my place in the world, just stability and everything gone, finances gone."Vince McMahon resigned from WWE after the allegations surfacedAt the start of 2024, WWE announced that Vince McMahon had sold the company to Endeavor Group, the parent company of UFC. Both entities were merged to form the new TKO Group Holdings, with McMahon holding a key position on the board. However, after the allegations surfaced, McMahon re-signed from the company, with TKO wiping him out of the records of the same company he created over four decades ago.After his exit, McMahon rarely made public appearances and reportedly started a new company, '13&I', which has yet to begin operations as of this writing. articles.title: Man Utd's Gabriel in limbo

articles.body:
Had the situation worked out differently, 15-year-old JJ Gabriel would have been preparing for his Manchester United debut tonight and potentially becoming the club's youngest player.

Instead, the young forward is in limbo, having asked United for his registration to be cancelled , which would allow him to join one of the many clubs across Europe who are very keen to sign him.

The crux of the issue goes back to what he feels were promises that have been made around a pathway to the first team, specifically in pre-season, that weren't honoured – Gabriel was part of four squads but only featured for eight minutes. He travelled to Norway for the meeting with Rosenborg on 24 July but didn't get on, even though head coach Michael Carrick made 11 substitutions - including five players who have since left the club, either on loan or permanently.

Then Gabriel was not registered for the Champions League encounter with Sabah FK last week. He would have needed to have been on Uefa's A list of players, but was omitted, even though Manuel Ugarte – who is injured and won't be available until after the league phase when players can be re-registered - and 18-year-old new arrival Tynan Thompson, were named.

So, while United sources are adamant it was intended Gabriel would have been involved against Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, sources close to him had no confidence he would actually get on the pitch.

United say they feel the situation can be rectified, and chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are involved. They also say they will not release Gabriel from his registration, which runs to the end of the season.

It will be interesting to see how the situation unfolds.
